questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: main branch, reviewing the User Dashboard UI plan.
ELI10: gstack routes requests to the right skill more reliably when CLAUDE.md has a short routing section. This is one-time setup, separate from the design review. We're in plan mode, so if you pick A the CLAUDE.md edit and commit wait until plan mode ends.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Without rules you invoke skills by hand; with them, CLAUDE.md gains a section and a commit.
Recommendation: A because routing is a one-time setup that saves manual invocations later.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Add routing rules (recommended)
  ✅ Future requests like 'review this plan' auto-route to the right gstack skill
  ✅ One-time change, a short appended section at the end of CLAUDE.md
  ❌ Edits and commits CLAUDE.md, deferred here because plan mode is read-only
B) No thanks
  ✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as it is, no commit added to the repo
  ✅ Nothing to defer, review continues with zero side effects
  ❌ You keep invoking skills manually by slash command every time
Net: small one-time repo edit vs. manual skill invocation.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description: Append the skill routing section to CLAUDE.md and commit (deferred until plan mode ends).

options.label: No thanks
options.description: Set routing_declined and invoke skills manually.

questions.question:
D2 — Review focus: all 7 dimensions or specific areas?
Project/branch/task: main branch, User Dashboard plan (review-input.md).
ELI10: I rated this plan 5/10 on design completeness. The biggest gaps are information hierarchy and layout per breakpoint, row anatomy and empty-state content, and modal/toast accessibility details. I'll generate visual mockups next, then review all 7 dimensions unless you want me to narrow the focus.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Narrowing skips dimensions, which the implementer then guesses at.
Recommendation: A because the gaps span hierarchy, states, a11y and visual spec, so a partial pass leaves holes.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10
Pros / cons:
A) All 7 dimensions (recommended)
  ✅ Every gap gets its own decision, so the implementer has nothing left to guess
  ✅ Catches issues across dimensions such as mobile order versus a11y focus order
  ❌ More questions, one per gap, so the review takes longer (human: ~1 hr / CC: ~15 min)
B) Focus on hierarchy, states and accessibility only
  ✅ Fewer decisions and a faster path to an implementable plan for this dashboard
  ✅ Targets the three areas where the plan is currently weakest
  ❌ Visual tokens, AI-slop risk and unresolved decisions go unreviewed
Net: thoroughness versus a faster, narrower pass.

options.label: All 7 dimensions (recommended)
options.description: Full review: hierarchy, states, journey, AI slop, design system, responsive/a11y, unresolved decisions.

options.label: Hierarchy, states, a11y
options.description: Narrow review to the three weakest areas.

questions.question:
D3 — Want outside design voices before the detailed review?
Project/branch/task: main branch, User Dashboard plan, text-only review (designer has no API key).
ELI10: Before the 7 passes I can bring in two independent reviewers: Codex checks the plan against hard design rules and a litmus scorecard, and a fresh Claude subagent does a completeness read. That gives a second opinion on hierarchy and AI-slop risk.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skipping means one reviewer's judgment; running costs a few minutes.
Recommendation: A because with no mockups to anchor on, a cross-model check adds signal — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Yes, run outside design voices (recommended)
  ✅ Codex hard-rule + litmus scorecard plus an independent Claude completeness read
  ✅ Disagreements surface with both perspectives in the relevant pass
  ❌ Adds a few minutes; Codex may be missing here, in which case only the Claude voice runs and it's tagged single-model
B) No, proceed without
  ✅ Straight into the 7 passes with the plan text as anchor, since mockups were unavailable
  ✅ Fewest steps to a fixed plan
  ❌ Findings rest on one reviewer; no cross-model check on slop risk or hierarchy
Net: a cross-model check versus speed.

options.label: Yes, run outside design voices (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Codex hard-rule + litmus scorecard plus an independent Claude completeness read. ✅ Disagreements surface with both perspectives in the relevant pass. ❌ Adds a few minutes; Codex may be missing here, in which case only the Claude voice runs and it's tagged single-model.

options.label: No, proceed without
options.description: ✅ Straight into the 7 passes with the approved mockup as anchor. ✅ Fewest steps to a fixed plan. ❌ Findings rest on one reviewer; no cross-model check on slop risk or hierarchy.

questions.question:
D4 — Search learnings from your other projects too?
Project/branch/task: main branch, User Dashboard design review.
ELI10: gstack can look for lessons it saved in your other local projects and apply them here. The data never leaves your machine. This project has no saved learnings yet.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Cross-project can carry one client's patterns into another; project-only misses useful past lessons.
Recommendation: A because solo developers benefit from reused patterns and nothing leaves the machine.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
  ✅ Past dashboard/modal pitfalls from other repos can show up in this review
  ✅ Stays fully local, one config flag you can flip back anytime
  ❌ Patterns from unrelated client codebases could bleed into this project's advice
B) Keep learnings project-scoped only
  ✅ Strict separation between codebases, safest for client or agency work
  ✅ Advice is grounded only in this repo's own history
  ❌ This repo has zero learnings so far, so nothing gets reused today
Net: reuse across projects versus strict isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: Set cross_project_learnings true and search all local projects.

questions.question:
D5 — Issue 1: Dashboard hierarchy and layout per breakpoint
Project/branch/task: main branch, User Dashboard plan, Pass 1 (Information Architecture).
ELI10: Users land here right after login, scan for a second, and either act or leave. The plan doesn't say which panel wins that second or how the three panels sit on phone versus desktop. Principle: every screen has a hierarchy; if everything competes, nothing wins.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Unread notifications get buried below a long activity feed, or the page ships as a generic 3-card grid.
Recommendation: 1A because notifications are the only actionable content; quick actions are just two links and fit the page header without needing their own panel.
Completeness: 1A=9/10, 1B=8/10, 1C=4/10
Pros / cons:
A) Action-first: header row + Notifications main, Activity rail (recommended)
  ✅ Page header: 'Dashboard' h1 with the two quick-action links at its right (wrapping below on mobile)
  ✅ lg: Notifications in a ~2/3 main column, Recent activity ~1/3 rail; md/sm: single column, Notifications then Activity
  ❌ Quick actions lose a standalone 'panel', so its empty/loading states mostly disappear (QuickActions is static config)
B) Activity-first: Activity main column, Notifications right rail
  ✅ Reads like a timeline home, good if activity is what users came for
  ✅ Keeps the three components as separate panels exactly as named in the plan
  ❌ Unread notifications sit in a narrow rail and drop below the activity feed on mobile
C) Equal three-panel grid, stacked on mobile
  ✅ Simplest Tailwind layout (grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3) with almost nothing to specify
  ✅ Each panel gets identical treatment, so there are fewer one-off styles
  ❌ Generic SaaS card mosaic with no lead content: an AI-slop hard-rejection pattern
Net: actionable-first hierarchy versus a timeline-first or flat layout.

options.label: 1A Action-first (recommended)
options.description: Header row with quick-action links; Notifications main column, Activity rail on lg; single column Notifications then Activity on sm/md.

options.label: 1B Activity-first
options.description: Activity main column, Notifications right rail; mobile Activity then Notifications.

options.label: 1C Equal 3-panel grid
options.description: Three equal panels on md+, stacked on mobile.
